access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3481) from the LOC reference images. Young working women of New York in their own street clothes in the winter of the 1909 shirtwaist strike: dark skirts to the ankle, clear of the ground, shirtwaists with tall standing collars, one with a dark bow tie at the collar, a dark belt with a buckle over the skirt's top; coats and broad hats over them for the cold. Five years after the scene date and of New York, not Chicago; read for what a young working woman wore in the street, not for any person.
note: A reference picture for the 1904 parlor maid's street dress, Christine Nelson of the Glessner household (data/humans/recipes/errand_1904.json).
what_it_supplies: a young working woman's street dress of the decade: shirtwaist with a tall collar, a bow tie, a belt, a dark skirt clear of the ground at the ankle
what_it_does_not_supply: the summer hat of 1904 (these are winter hats of 1909)
anything about Chicago, the Glessner household or Christine Nelson; no likeness is asserted
